items.title: For Trans-Neptunian Objects, The Past Is Written On Their Surface
items.summary: James Webb discovered surface colors reveal whether distant icy bodies formed near the Sun or beyond Neptune, preserving their formation history.

items.title: Archaea as 'flexitarians': Ammonia-oxidizing microbes also feed on amino acids
items.source: Biology News - Evolution, Cell theory, Gene theory, Microbiology, Biotechnology
items.summary: Marine archaea confirmed to eat amino acids, not just ammonia—revealing flexible diet and hidden symbiotic communication with host sponges.

items.title: One unexplained event could hint at heavy dark matter
items.source: Physics News - Physics News, Material Sciences, Science News, Physics
items.summary: LUX-ZEPLIN experiment reports unexplained signal that may hint at heavy dark matter detection—potential breakthrough in hunt for invisible matter.

items.title: Levitated magnet opens new frontier in search for ultraheavy dark matter
items.source: Physics News - Physics News, Material Sciences, Science News, Physics
items.summary: Magnetically levitated particle used as ultra-sensitive detector to search for ultraheavy dark matter, extending the mass range of particles scientists can hunt for.

items.title: Ancient “living fossils” may reveal how complex life began
items.summary: First direct images show an ancient archaeon physically connected to bacteria, exchanging nutrients—a rare snapshot of how the first complex cells may have formed billions of years ago.

items.title: Dark matter detector finds a strange signal scientists can’t yet explain
items.summary: LUX-ZEPLIN experiment detects rare, unexplained particle interaction consistent with dark matter; single candidate event, awaiting confirmation from future data.

items.title: A mysterious signal around Earth could be dark matter
items.summary: Earth's magnetic field used as planet-scale dark matter detector; new limits set on ultralight axions and unexplained dark photon signals detected.

items.title: Scientists Intrigued by a Surprising Result in the Search for Dark Matter
items.summary: Deep underground detector records anomalous particle interaction unexplained by known physics; too early to confirm dark matter but intriguing candidate event.

items.title: SuperCDMS SNOLAB Starts Its Dark Matter Hunt
items.summary: SuperCDMS SNOLAB dark matter detector begins scientific operations, hunting for direct detection of lightweight dark matter particles underground.

items.title: Have we finally found dark matter?
items.summary: LUX-ZEPLIN dark matter detector reports first direct evidence of WIMP particle; unexplained signal matches long-sought dark matter candidate.

items.title: Is this the first glimpse of dark matter? Data point excites physicists
items.summary: Particle physics experiment detects unexplained energy signal consistent with dark matter WIMP candidate; first direct evidence of candidate particle interaction.

items.title: Planetary gas gaps and kinematic signatures in the planet forming disk around WISPIT 2
items.summary: ALMA observations directly detect gas gaps and kinematic signatures matching known giant protoplanets in planet-forming disk; bridges planet formation theory to observation.

items.title: A Homogeneous Survey of JWST MIRI Transmission Spectra of 10 Exoplanets
items.summary: JWST survey finds hints of complex molecules in atmospheres of temperate sub-Neptune exoplanets; confirms spectral features are real, not instrumental noise.

items.title: JWST Excludes Exomoons Down to 0.1 Earth Radii Around a Rocky, Temperate Exoplanet
items.summary: JWST's deepest exomoon search rules out Earth-sized moons around temperate rocky planet; excludes analogs to many Solar System moons.

items.title: Evidence for LP 890-9d via Transit Timing Variations
items.summary: JWST detects timing variations suggesting third rocky exoplanet around nearby star LP 890-9; candidate requires confirmation with additional observations.

items.title: Microwave-Induced Optomagnetism in High-Temperature Superconductors
items.summary: First observation of microwave-driven magnetic effect in high-temperature superconductor film; enables contactless magnetic control in quantum systems.

items.title: Direct Validation of Superconductivity through Contact-Free Detection of Persistent Supercurrents Using Room-Temperature Quantum Magnetometry
items.summary: New room-temperature technique validates superconductivity in tiny samples by detecting persistent currents without electrical contacts, enabling fast screening of high-pressure superconductor candidates.

items.title: A Clearer View of HAT-P-1 b: JWST NIRSpec G395H Reveals Water, Carbon Dioxide, and Possibly Hydrogen Sulfide
items.summary: JWST directly detected water, carbon dioxide, and possibly hydrogen sulfide in hot Jupiter atmosphere; demonstrates first high-resolution molecular inventory across infrared enabling new insights into exoplanet composition.

items.title: Two-dimensional quantum Griffith singularity in three-dimensional ZrN superconducting films
items.summary: First observation of 2D quantum critical behavior in 3D superconducting films; reveals disorder-driven phase transitions and rare-region effects near superconductor-insulator boundary.

items.title: Real-time virtual circuits for plasma shape control via neural network emulators: experimental demonstration on MAST Upgrade
items.summary: Real-time AI-based plasma shape control validated on MAST Upgrade tokamak; replaces manual schedules with live neural network predictions, simplifying tokamak operation.

items.title: Scientists stunned by signs of ancient life in a place no one expected
items.summary: Ancient seafloor rocks in Morocco show microbial mat structures (wrinkles) formed in darkness hundreds of feet below ocean surface—reveals deep-ocean chemosynthetic ecosystems were more widespread than thought.

items.title: A new recipe unlocks “impossible” nanocrystals for LEDs, implants, and superconductors
items.summary: Lab synthesis of previously impossible metal-nitride nanocrystals; enables new flexible electronics and superconductor device architectures once scarce materials now producible.

items.title: NASA’s Roman Telescope Takes Aim at Cosmic Mysteries
items.summary: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched aboard SpaceX Falcon Heavy; now traveling to Lagrange Point 2 to study exoplanets, dark energy, and dark matter.

items.title: Planets Hurry To Form Before the Protoplanetary Disk Dissipates
items.summary: JWST/MIRI observations reveal how magnetic jets and photoevaporative winds clear gas from planet-forming disks over time.

items.title: James Webb Space Telescope observes 72 stars and finds planet formation is a race against time
items.summary: James Webb study of 72 young stars reveals planets form in tight race against disk gas dispersal; new understanding of planet formation timescales.

items.title: One Tiny Chemical Difference in RNA Could Help Explain the Origins of Life
items.summary: RNA's chemical advantage in forming droplets under heat and acidity illuminates how early life molecules could self-organize before cells existed.

items.title: How fusion reactions can survive flaws—up to a point
items.source: Physics News - Physics News, Material Sciences, Science News, Physics
items.summary: Lab finding shows inertial fusion fuel targets tolerate imperfections up to a threshold; informs practical design of future fusion reactors.

items.title: Deep underground, SuperCDMS begins hunting light dark matter with 24 cryogenic crystals
items.source: Physics News - Physics News, Material Sciences, Science News, Physics
items.summary: SuperCDMS deep-underground detector begins first scientific data collection in hunt for light dark matter particles using ultrasensitive cryogenic crystals.

items.title: Meteorite that smashed through a New Jersey roof reveals clues to life’s origins
items.summary: Meteorite recovered from New Jersey contains ancient salty fluids, organic compounds, and amino acids from a primitive asteroid—evidence that space rocks delivered life's building blocks to early Earth.

items.title: On Cloud 9: Have astronomers discovered the first starless galaxy?
items.summary: Astronomers close to confirming first galaxy with virtually no stars but packed with dark matter and gas—reveals unexpected galaxy formation pathway.

items.title: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Telescope launches to space
items.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches to orbit; advanced infrared coronagraph enables direct exoplanet imaging and dark energy studies.

items.title: An Inverse Grad-Shafranov Neural Network Approach to Tokamak Magnetic Control
items.summary: AI-based inverse plasma shaping control demonstrated on TCV tokamak; neural network learns real-time magnetic coil commands, enabling flexible plasma control with fewer diagnostics.

items.title: First Plasma Commissioning and Operational Highlights from India's First Spherical Tokamak at IPR
items.summary: India's first spherical tokamak achieves first plasma; new low-cost fusion research platform commissioned for non-inductive startup and plasma physics studies.

items.title: Magnetic field first kills superconductor, then brings it back to life
items.summary: Ultrathin material exhibits rare re-entrant superconductivity—superconductivity returns after magnetic field suppresses it—opening new physics in 2D superconductors.

items.title: Scientists Melted A Diamond and Cracked a Secret of Ice Giants
items.summary: Lab experiment mimics diamond-rain process in ice giants for first time; physics may improve fusion energy output by threefold.

items.title: The JWST/NIRCam Scattered Light Disks GTO 2780 program: panchromatic coronagraphic imaging of the HD 10647, HD 32297, HD 61005, HD 107146, and HD 181327 debris disk systems
items.summary: JWST first coronagraphic images of five debris-disk systems reveal water ice and dust structure at unprecedented infrared resolution and detail.

items.title: Diamond quantum-sensing platform with integrated boron-doped diamond microwave antenna and thermometer
items.summary: Integrated diamond quantum sensor platform combines nitrogen-vacancy centers with microwave antenna and thermometer on one chip—enabling precise cryogenic magnetic imaging of superconductors.

items.title: Scalable, Simple, and Versatile Encapsulation of 2D Materials and Devices
items.summary: New encapsulation method using aluminum oxide preserves superconducting properties in fragile 2D materials while simplifying device fabrication—enabling practical quantum material devices.
